name: Battle Ropes
description: Battle ropes are a conditioning exercise in which the athlete alternates or simultaneously waves heavy ropes anchored at one end, sustaining powerful arm and shoulder drive patterns for a timed interval. The continuous undulating motion of the ropes requires sustained explosive upper body work while the lower body is maintained in a stable athletic stance, creating high metabolic demand. Battle rope training is used for upper body power endurance, cardiovascular conditioning, and grip strength.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing the anchor point with feet shoulder-width apart in an athletic squat stance, one rope end in each hand. Slight hip hinge, slight knee bend.
execution.setup_instructions: Anchor a heavy rope (38–50mm diameter) at a fixed point. Stand at a distance that keeps the rope slightly slack. Maintain a consistent athletic stance throughout.
steps: Step 1: Hold one rope end in each hand with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Begin alternating waves: drive the right arm up and immediately bring it down while driving the left arm up.
Step 3: Keep the waves large and continuous — the rope should form visible undulations moving toward the anchor.
Step 4: Maintain an athletic stance throughout — do not let the torso collapse or the knees straighten.
Step 5: Continue for the prescribed duration at maximum sustainable effort.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously at a rhythm matching the work rate. Do not hold breath.
common_mistakes: Standing up too tall — the athletic stance with hips back keeps the core engaged
Letting the waves die — maintain large, powerful waves throughout
Only moving from the elbows — the motion should initiate from the shoulders
safety_considerations: High demand on the shoulders and forearms — adequate warm-up required.
Build interval duration progressively — do not start at full intensity with long intervals.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Large amplitude waves — full shoulder range. Rope must reach the anchor on each wave.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Typically performed for 20–40 second intervals with equal rest. 5–8 rounds.
coaching_cues: Drive from the shoulder — not just the elbow
